newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Mobutu's health again at top of Zaire's worries.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu's health again at top of Zaire's worries.

text.p: Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko flies to France on Thursday to consult doctors about his health amid the growing crisis in the Central African nation where rebels control a strip of territory in the east.
Mobutu will return to his villa in the south of France for consultations with doctors, his spokesman told Reuters.

Since coming home three weeks ago, Mobutu effected a major reshuffle in the government and the army high command in preparation for an intended counter-attack on positions held by rebels who have seized a large tract of eastern Zaire.
The rebels, led by longtime Mobutu opponent Laurent Kabila, have vowed to march to Kinshasa to overthrow Mobutu, who has ruled the mineral-rich country for 31 years.
Mobutu flies from his jungle palace at Gbadolite where he has stayed for much of the time since returning on December 17 from months of cancer treatment and rest in Europe.
"He is leaving tommorrow for health reasons, and in relation to consultations he is due to have with his doctors," spokesman Kabuya Lumuna said on Wednesday.
In France the office of the prefect (government representative) in the French Riviera capital said Mobutu's private flight would land at midday at Nice airport.
The official said Mobutu had an open-ended visa.
Mobutu returned to Kinshasa in December to a huge welcome by well over 100,000 inhabitants of the capital.

But it was a short hour of glory, as Zaire's ruler of 31 years has drawn renewed attacks from political enemies since retaining much criticised Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo at the head of a new crisis government formed on Christmas Eve.
The rebels have thrust out from the North and South Kivu area they originally controlled and fighting has raged around the eastern town of Bunia in Upper Zaire.
The alliance that began the rebellion with a group of mostly ethnic Tutsis now occupies a 500 km (300 mile) swath of eastern Zaire along the border with Rwanda, Burundi and Uganda.
Mobutu has ruled out negotiation with rebel leader Kabila and vowed to crush him. But analysts say Zaire is not in a position to inflict heavy losses on the better-equipped rebels.

A much trumpeted counter-attack against the ethnic Tutsi rebels, who Zaire says are backed by Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi, has so far failed to materialise with the Ziare's retreating army plagued by problems of discipline.
On Wednesday the rebels called on France, Belgium, South Africa and others to stop their citizens joining a mercenary force the rebels say is supporting the army.

"We want to dissuade these countries from allowing their people to serve a criminal and prolong his stay in power," the rebels' foreign affairs spokesman Kakudji Gaetan told a news conference in Goma.
Kakudji said mercenaries from France, Belgium, South Africa, Angola and Togo were being assembled by Mobutu along with soldiers of the Hutu former Rwandan army in exile in Zaire.
